page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top centre. Page number at the top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot. Left margin carries printed "„" line marks, which are not text and are not transcribed.

main_text.l: mortis obierit. Tertiò, Johannes Keplerus & Dio-
nysius Petavius eam lunæ eclipsin intelligunt, quæ accidit
anno Juliano xlii Martii d. xiii. Hor. 2.
min. 45. &c. à mediâ nocte. Fuit tunc, referente
Petavio de Doct. Temp. libr. xi: 1. verus locus
solis in piscium gradu 20. m. 24. Desiit H. 4. M. 9.
Duratio fuit horarum 2. m. 47. ac digitos sex
ferè defecit. Quarto Johannes Georgius Herwart
ab Hohenburgh, in nova, verâ, & exactè ad calculum
astronomicum revocatâ Chronologiâ, quam vocat
cap. 149. pag. 75. eandem eclipsin refert ad
annum Christi vulgarem septimum, quem vocat, (eundemque
nos secundum epochæ vulgaris dicimus,
Julianum xlvii, annum urbis Varronianum finientem
754.) cujus die 20 Febr. sole in 29 gradu,
min. 51 seu fine aquarii versante, luna Hierosolymis
horâ unâ ferè ante noctis medium defecit digitis
21 min. 18. Quinto D. Wilhelmus Langius
libr. 2. de annis Christi, cap. 18. eam intelligit eclipsin
lunæ, quæ accidcrit anno Iul. xliv. Ian. d. 70[?], cujus
finis Arbelis, visus est, ac in locis orientalibus
medium. Defecit vero luna dig. 7. m. 33. Incepit
deficere Arbelis horâ post meridiem 4. m. 8, finita
est Hor. 5. m. 8. quadrante ferè horæ post solis
occasum. Ideoque commodè illic propter refractio-
nem 33 min. visa fuit. Atque huic eclipsi, quam
eodem tempore contigisse Nicolaus ab Assyriis[?]
audiverat, effecta illa, graviaque symptomata, quæ
Herodi contigerunt, tribuit Josephus. Sexto denique
Josephus Scaliger libr. 5. de Emend. Temp. pag.
463. eclipsin Lunæ, à Iudaicæ historiæ scriptore
annotatam, accidisse autumat anno Iul. xlv Ian. viii

page.notes: Printed "„" marks in the left margin are line or quotation marks, not text, and are not transcribed. Word-break hyphen at "Dio-nysius" kept as printed. The final word is cut at the page foot, "me-" with its printed hyphen; the catchword "dia" completes it. Doubtful readings: "Ian. d. 70" (the 70 may be a misprint or a misread numeral); "Assyriis" (the scan's long s is faint and the printed form could be read as "Alfyriis"; read as Assyriis); "Iul. xliv" read as printed. A printer's mark after "Nicolaus" (a small asterisk-like sign) was not transcribed as text. Italic is marked on names and cited phrases; the exact extent of italic in some phrases is uncertain.
